questions.problem: Find the volume of the cube whose sides each have length $7\,\text{cm}.$
questions.worked_solution:
The volume $V$ of a cube can be found using the formula

$$
V={s}^{3},
$$

where $s$ is the side length of the cube.

Substituting $s=7\,\text{cm}$ into the formula, we get 

$$
V=(7\,\text{cm})^{3}=343\,{\text{cm}}^{3}.
$$

canonical_examples.problem: The volume of a cube is $729\, \textrm{cm}^3.$ Find the length of the edges of the cube.
canonical_examples.worked_solution:
Since the volume of a cube is 

$$
V = s^3,
$$

where $s$ is the length of an edge, we can find $s$ as follows:

$$
s = \sqrt[3]{V} =  \sqrt[3]{729} = 9
$$

Therefore, the length of the edges is $9\,\textrm{cm}.$

canonical_examples.problem: Six identical plastic cubic containers have a combined volume of $48 \: \textrm{ft}^3.$ Find the side length of a single container.
canonical_examples.worked_solution:
First, we find the volume of a single container: 

$$
\dfrac{48 \: \textrm{ft}^3}{6} = 8 \: \textrm{ft}^3
$$

Now, we need to find the side length of one container. 

Since the volume of a cube is 

$$
V = s^3,
$$

where $s$ is the length of a side, we can find $s$ as follows:

$$
s = \sqrt[3]{V} = \sqrt[3]{8} = 2
$$

Therefore, the length of a side of a single container is $2\,\textrm{ft}.$

tutorials.name: Introduction
tutorials.problem:
Suppose that we have a cube whose edges are $2\,\textrm{cm}$ in length, like the one shown below. 

![](/home/jake/Developer/Course_Academy/reference/mathacademy/capture/differential/14224461/assets/b974b6e782801fbe2099971afd0df9a5c6e05a10afc2ce0e4054c850088e753b.png)

The formula for the volume $V$ of a cube with sides of length $s$ is given by

$$
V = s^3.
$$

To find the volume of this cube, we substitute $s=2 \: \textrm{cm}$ into the formula. This gives

$$
V = (2\, \textrm{cm})^3 = 8 \text{ cm}^3 .
$$

So the volume of the cube is $8\,\textrm{cm}^3.$
